editorial.purpose_and_first_use: The plain title introduces analysing a Centrale Rischi for a client meeting. The lesson covers supplying files, confirming company, period and meanings, running the current workflow, reading its main outputs and requesting a subsequent update. No narrow exception replaces the complete first-use sequence.
editorial.inputs_and_request: The fictional Officina Arco export contains nine bank/category/month rows for January through March, with declared column meanings, two banks and EUR. The request asks for March, a comparison with the previous months, a dashboard, workbook and meeting summary. The kit explicitly uses a normalized export; it explains original digital PDF intake without claiming the lesson executed that route.
editorial.execution_and_checkpoints: The actual native workflow checks the selected inputs and reviewed mapping, calculates all supplied periods, reconciles the latest total and validates the commentary evidence references. The checkpoints ask the learner to confirm files and current month, open the generated result, trace a bank to the input rows and identify what to supply next time. The authoring fixtures exercise the normal Codex interpretation stage; they are not shipped lesson answers or recorded professional approvals.
editorial.deliverable_and_next_action: The native dashboard and report contain the current totals, category comparison, duration breakdown, specific observations and two useful follow-up questions. The workbook has Italian headers and fixed statuses, typed numeric values, source-row traceability and separate coverage messages for missing evidence versus no reported events. All sheets were visually reviewed through the native workbook import. The delivery card links the actual report and workbook; it no longer presents an empty issue template as completed work. The report remains a draft for professional review.
editorial.practice_and_repeat: The learner asks for April using the supplied twelve-row update. A separate native run in the same engagement reports April and its March comparison, leaving all March output bytes unchanged. The lesson finishes by explaining how to repeat for a client with a digital original or verified export, a period and an objective.
editorial.language_and_pacing: Italian is the supported output language of this workflow. The complete lesson, fictional contexts, primary workbook labels and authored commentary use Italian. Six stages total 390 seconds. The guided reading focuses on the headline result, one traced bank and the questions while the full detail remains available. Processing and user questions may extend elapsed time; the duration has not been measured with a learner.

demo.result_review: March used exposure is EUR 119000 against EUR 170000 operational facilities, with EUR 51000 calculated margin. Monthly totals are 128000, 128000 and 119000; the EUR 9000 fall splits into 6000, 2000 and 1000 by category. Levante accounts for 68.91 percent and EUR 82000. The source supports the described balances, not their business causes. Missing prejudicial and financial evidence remains unavailable; no rating, DSCR or readily drawable liquidity is inferred.

practice.result_review: The new April run shows EUR 117000 used, EUR 53000 calculated margin and a EUR 2000 monthly decline. Revoca and scadenza each fall by 2000 while autoliquidante increases by 2000. Levante remains EUR 80000, 68.38 percent. The earlier March run remains byte-identical. The actual April commentary, report, workbook and delivery note preserve review status and source limits.
